name: Every operator and verifier list change is audited
summary: operators add|remove and verifiers add|remove take --actor OPERATOR and --reason TEXT (at most 400 characters; blank refused); restore-new takes both for its --restore-operators/--restore-verifiers re-grants. A real list change appends one entry - at, operator, list, actor, change, reason - to the runtime-level authority-changes.audit.json beside deployment.private.json (schema_version 1, mode 0600, newest 200 kept; drops said on stderr), under the lock and BEFORE the configuration. A re-grant records one entry per name, operator from restore-new --actor or null, reason naming restore-new and the source. The read-only authority-changes prints the entries (operator-null ones marked and counted), the current lists, and a replay saying when the trail does not lead to them. A damaged audit never refuses a REMOVAL: the file is set aside as .damaged-STAMP and a fresh history records that; an ADD is refused with the recovery named; a directory, fifo or symlink is refused. Unknown entry fields, a schema_version that is true or 1.0, and repeated --actor/--reason are refused. NOT covered, with nothing detecting it: a hand edit of deployment.private.json; a list change by an older kit.
